You can disable the new OpenCode logo sound/animation trigger by turning off mouse support in the TUI. 
At the moment, there is no dedicated sound or logo animation config flag, so this is the best permanent workaround.
1. Create or edit `~/.config/opencode/tui.json`
2. Add:
```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/tui.json",
  "mouse": false
}
```

This prevents accidental logo clicks (which trigger the burst + sound effect).

I can confirm this bug. Based on my testing with a clangd proxy, I would like to supplement the technical analysis. Please fix these bugs in the following way:

1. Update the Tool Schema: **Remove filePath, line, and character** from the "**required**" list for the workspaceSymbol operation. Instead, make a "query" (string) parameter mandatory.

2. Pass the Argument: Ensure that the actual query string provided by the model is passed into the lsp.workspaceSymbol(query) call instead of the current hardcoded empty string.

3. Align with LSP Specification: Ensure the tool follows the standard WorkspaceSymbolParams as defined in the official [Microsoft LSP 3.17 Specification](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/).

Since workspace/symbol is a global search by design, it should not be architecturally tied to a specific file path or coordinates. This adjustment will allow the LLM to perform proper project-wide discovery, which is critical for identifying symbols definitions across the entire repo / project.

Also asked AI to figure something out and got this:

## The Problem
Opencode hangs at "build · [model]" when using `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` custom providers.
The API works via curl, but opencode never receives/processes the response.
## Confirmed Working
- ✅ curl to API endpoint
- ✅ SDK standalone test (non-streaming)
- ✅ opencode built-in models (opencode/minimax-m2.5-free)
## Not Working
- ❌ opencode with @ai-sdk/openai-compatible (any model, any provider)
- ❌ All 3 reported issues (#23094, #22132, #11056) have same symptoms
## Root Cause Hypothesis
The issue is NOT in:
- Network connectivity (curl works)
- API authentication (standalone SDK works)
- Model configuration (works with built-in models)
The issue IS in:
- How opencode processes the streaming response from @ai-sdk/openai-compatible
- OR how the SDK handles the response in the opencode context
## Evidence
1. Logs show: `llm providerID=RuAPI ... stream`
2. Then: `session.updated publishing`
3. Then: HANGS - no error, no timeout, no response
## Things That Didn't Fix It
- Adding apiKey to config
- Adding timeout to config  
- Adding bunfig.toml (workaround for different issue)
- Different SDK versions (1.0.0, 2.0.41)
- Different models (claude-opus, gpt-5.4, claude-sonnet)
- Different provider options
## What Would Help Debug
1. Network trace showing if request is made and if response is received
2. Comparing working builtin model vs broken custom provider at code level
3. SDK version compatibility with opencode version
## Related Issues (all same root cause - likely)
- #23094 - RuAPI provider (my case)
- #22132 - Ollama provider  
- #11056 - Venice provider
## For Developers
The fix needs to be in opencode's LLM response handling for 
@ai-sdk/openai-compatible providers. The SDK itself works fine.

Additional isolation results from local debugging:

1) Baseline stable condition:
- Fully reset desktop state directories:
  - ~/Library/Application Support/ai.opencode.desktop
  - ~/Library/Caches/ai.opencode.desktop
  - ~/Library/WebKit/ai.opencode.desktop
- Start with an empty opencode.db (no projects/sessions/messages/parts)
- Desktop remains stable (WebContent ~160MB, sidecar ~500MB, no runaway growth over 20s)

2) Trigger condition:
- Reintroducing old session/history data can re-trigger runaway memory growth in Desktop startup (WebContent multi-GB in ~10-20s)
- In bad states, sidecar also spikes transiently (1-3GB), and UI becomes effectively unusable/frozen

3) Current workaround that restored usability:
- Keep fresh desktop state reset
- Keep only project metadata (global + bona-hero) and **no historical sessions**
- Let user create fresh sessions

4) Data integrity note:
- During one failing cycle, opencode.db showed sqlite integrity errors (later replaced with healthy backup)

This suggests desktop renderer startup is sensitive to specific historical session payload/state combinations, not only snapshot errors.

Confirmed fix: adding `\"external_directory\": \"allow\"` to the agent's `permission` block solved it. Write tool completed in 2.0s and file was created on disk.

Setting just `edit` and `write` to `allow` was insufficient — the external directory check is a separate permission key that specifically governs writes outside WORKDIR. Fully our config bug, not OpenCode.

Full working block:
```json
"permission": {
  "edit": "allow",
  "write": "allow",
  "bash": "allow",
  "external_directory": "allow"
}
```

New findings by another user on reddit:

> Fair concern, and it's one I had too before digging into how Moonshot's backend actually routes.
> 
> Short version: for kimi-for-coding specifically, the model isn't selected by the id string in the request body. It's selected by the auth token type. Static `sk-kimi-...` API keys land you on K2.5. OAuth JWTs with `scope: kimi-code` (what Kimi CLI uses) land you on K2.6. The `model` field on the wire is basically cosmetic, the backend decides from the token.
> 
> That's also why the models.dev `kimi-for-coding` entry behaves the way it does. That one's wired to a static `KIMI_API_KEY` on an Anthropic-compatible path, which is the K2.5 code path. Different auth, different model, same id string. Easy to conflate.
> 
> The plugin I'm building does the OAuth device flow the same way Kimi CLI does, so by construction it's on the K2.6 path. It also hits `GET /coding/v1/models` at login and on every token refresh and rewrites the wire `model` field to whatever the server hands back (mirrors kimi-cli's `refresh_managed_models`). The `X-Msh-*` headers and UA match kimi-cli exactly. If any of that drifts the backend 403s with `access_terminated_error` rather than silently downgrading, which is actually the nicer failure mode.
> 
> What nobody can control from the client side is whether Moonshot quietly swaps the weights behind kimi-for-coding or does traffic-shaping to something cheaper during peak hours. Kimi CLI is in the same boat. That's a Moonshot trust question, not an opencode one. The only real signal is eval drift over time, which is roughly what SanityHarness is already measuring anyway.
> 
> TL;DR: the id gets respected in the sense that K2.5 vs K2.6 is determined by your auth, and the OAuth plugin puts you on the K2.6 path deterministically. Whether Moonshot's K2.6 endpoint stays pointed at the same weights forever, can't promise that, and neither can they.
> 
> I have the plugin built now, and so far seems to be working well. This ended up being more work than I expected, but it's done now, and I stamped out the bugs I came across. This is a little bit more than just a "get k2.6" plugin, I aimed for kimi cli parity because the /coding endpoint has Kimi-specific extensions on top of the OpenAI-compatible shape that kimi cli actually uses, and I wanted those wired through properly instead of half-supported. That means the seven `X-Msh-*` headers and UA are pinned to kimi cli's exact values (anything off-spec there gets you 403'd as a non-coding-agent client), the reasoning effort switch maps to the `thinking` and `reasoning_effort` body fields the same way kimi cli maps them, `prompt_cache_key` is forwarded so multi-turn sessions actually hit the server-side cache, and the model id discovery/refresh dance matches `refresh_managed_models` so token refresh and account-type changes don't strand you on a stale id. Basically the goal was: if it works in kimi cli, it should work here, with the same wire behavior. [https://github.com/lemon07r/opencode-kimi-full/](https://github.com/lemon07r/opencode-kimi-full/)
